message.content: Priya says editors on shop.northwindtrust.org and careers.northwindtrust.org can't log in since yesterday, ticket NWT-4182. The main site northwind.example works. Login form just reloads.

content.text: The form reloads with: "Error: Cookies are blocked or not supported by your browser. You must enable cookies to use WordPress." I first checked whether the Varnish layer strips Set-Cookie on wp-login.php. It doesn't: `curl -sI https://shop.northwindtrust.org/wp-login.php` shows `set-cookie: wordpress_test_cookie=WP%20Cookie%20check; path=/; domain=.northwind.example; secure; HttpOnly`. The domain is wrong for that host, so the browser drops it.

message.content: where does that domain come from

content.text: wp-config.php line 41: `define( 'COOKIE_DOMAIN', '.northwind.example' );`, added in 2019 per git blame (commit by j.doe). The network is a subdomain install (`SUBDOMAIN_INSTALL` is true) with shop and careers mapped to their own domains. If we remove the define, WordPress falls back to host-only cookies on every site, so mapped domains will get cookies for their own host.

message.content: removed it on staging, both mapped sites log in fine now. ship it

content.text: Deployed to production in release 3.18.2. Priya confirmed editors on both mapped sites can log in. I did not test the `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']` variant, only the removal. Lockout hit roughly 30% of editors according to Priya's message, not counted.
